plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A fast-growing subtropical tree with fern-like leaves that erupts into dense clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. When the blooms fall they carpet streets and gardens in purple.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Southern Hemisphere (October to December)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in Australia, South Africa (Pretoria), and Argentina
plants.funFact: Pretoria is nicknamed the Jacaranda City because of its tens of thousands of jacaranda trees, and a local superstition says a bloom falling on your head brings good luck.

plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: A shrub whose showy 'flowers' are actually colored bracts surrounding tiny yellow true flowers. In frost-free climates it blooms outdoors, and elsewhere it is a popular holiday potted plant.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (November to February) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to Mexico; grown outdoors in Mexico, Central America, southern California, Florida, and as a houseplant worldwide
plants.funFact: Poinsettias are short-day plants, needing about 12 hours of uninterrupted darkness each night for roughly eight weeks to develop their colorful bracts.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub that is among the earliest camellias to flower, producing fragrant, delicate, often single or semi-double blooms with prominent golden stamens. It tolerates more sun than other camellias.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early winter (October to December)
plants.location: Native to Japan; cultivated in the southeastern United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is a relative of the tea plant (Camellia sinensis), and its seeds are pressed to make a culinary and cosmetic oil in Japan and China.

plants.name: Schlumbergera truncata
plants.description: An epiphytic cactus with flat, segmented stems tipped with a pointed claw-like edge. It produces tubular, asymmetrical flowers in clusters at the ends of the stems.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early winter (November to December)
plants.location: Native to the coastal mountains of southeastern Brazil; grown as a houseplant worldwide
plants.funFact: In the wild it grows on trees and rocks in cool, humid cloud forests, and it triggers its flowering in response to shorter days and cooler nights.
